findings.title: Detection/audit/cooldown emit bounds carry no percentile while every other timed rule uses p95
findings.description: ab5e/c7e3/b5fa ('WITHIN 100 ms'), a17e ('WITHIN 100 ms'), and d8a2 ('WITHIN 50 ms') state a bare millisecond bound with no statistical qualifier, whereas every other timed rule in the artifact specifies 'at the 95th percentile'. The numeric value is not ADR-deferred (the deferred markers on these lines cover the abuse/enumeration threshold, not the emit latency), so an engineer must implement and validate these bounds now. Without a percentile they cannot tell whether 100 ms is a hard ceiling over 100% of events or a p95, which selects a different measurement harness (max-over-window assertion vs percentile sampling) and a different SLO. Triggers and responses are otherwise concrete and detectable; the gap is purely in the measurement contract.
findings.recommendation: Append the same qualifier used elsewhere, e.g. 'emit a detection event WITHIN 100 ms at the 95th percentile', or state 'WITHIN 100 ms (hard ceiling, 100% of events)' if an absolute bound is intended. Apply consistently to ab5e, c7e3, a17e, b5fa, and the 50 ms variant in d8a2.

findings.title: Bare '[ADR deferred: BRD.01.08.daeb]' markers do not name the deferred quantity
findings.description: These four markers name only the ADR topic, unlike the well-formed siblings db78 ('— reputation-screen timeout'), 0b67 ('— code-space sizing'), 135e ('— retry ceiling'), 00b9 ('— high-utilization threshold'), and ee86 ('— numeric rate bound'), each of which spells out the deferred item. The bound actually deferred here (the anti-abuse submission-volume threshold for ab5e/b5fa, the anti-enumeration probe threshold for c7e3/d8a2, and the cooldown duration) is described in prose but absent from the marker, leaving the deferral implicit at the marker level.
findings.recommendation: Extend each bare marker to name the deferred quantity, e.g. '[ADR deferred: BRD.01.08.daeb — anti-abuse submission-volume threshold and cooldown]' and '[ADR deferred: BRD.01.08.daeb — anti-enumeration probe threshold and cooldown]', matching the explicit form already used for the other deferrals.

findings.title: 'p95' is the artifact's load-bearing measurable but is absent from the EARS glossary
findings.description: PRD §15 defines 'p95' as 'the 95th-percentile value of a measured distribution'. EARS uses 'at the 95th percentile' on nearly every §3 line and the 'p95' shorthand in §4 (EARS.01.04.e27b 'p95 < 50 ms', 4eec 'p95 < 500 ms') and its preamble, yet the EARS glossary omits the term. A reader of EARS alone has no in-document definition tying the §3 prose form to the §4 shorthand, and the two glossaries should agree. Term-drift-by-omission, not a contradiction.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'p95' (or '95th percentile') row to the EARS glossary matching the PRD §15 definition verbatim, noting the §3 prose form and §4 'p95' shorthand denote the same measure.
